subject: surgery
title: Surgical wound healing: phases, collagen dynamics and complications

steps.tx: Normal surgical **wound healing** is a coordinated biological cascade comprising four overlapping chronological phases: hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation and remodeling. Hemostasis initiates immediately with platelet plug formation and fibrin deposition, releasing platelet-derived growth factor and transforming growth factor-beta. The inflammatory phase peaks at forty-eight hours with neutrophil infiltration followed by macrophages, which orchestrate subsequent tissue debridement and angiogenesis.
steps.say: Normal surgical wound healing is a biological cascade comprising four overlapping chronological phases: hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation and remodeling. Hemostasis initiates immediately with platelet plugging and fibrin deposition, releasing growth factors. steps.tx: The proliferative phase is characterized by granulation tissue formation, driven by fibroblasts synthesizing **type three collagen** and proteoglycans alongside vascular endothelial growth factor-mediated angiogenesis. In the remodeling phase, matrix metalloproteinases degrade immature type three collagen, replacing it with stronger, organized type one collagen bundles cross-linked by lysyl oxidase. Wound tensile strength reaches only twenty percent at three weeks and plateaus at eighty percent of unwounded skin.
steps.say: The proliferative phase is characterized by granulation tissue formation, driven by fibroblasts synthesizing type three collagen alongside angiogenesis. In remodeling, matrix metalloproteinases replace immature type three collagen with organized type one collagen cross-linked by lysyl oxidase. Tensile strength plateaus at eighty percent of normal.

steps.tx: Pathological scarring results from excessive fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis. A **hypertrophic scar** remains confined within the boundaries of the original surgical incision and often regresses spontaneously over twelve to eighteen months. In contrast, a **keloid** grows aggressively beyond the original margins, lacks spontaneous regression, exhibits thick disorganized collagen bundles, and occurs predominantly in darkly pigmented individuals, having high recurrence after simple excision.

steps.tx: Acute abdominal **wound dehiscence** or burst abdomen typically manifests between postoperative days five and eight with a sudden serosanguinous pink discharge soaking the dressing. It reflects failure of the deep fascial closure, provoked by increased intra-abdominal pressure, obesity, malnutrition or technical suture breakage. When evisceration occurs, immediate management requires covering exposed bowel with sterile saline-soaked dressings and urgent return to the operating room.
